rg.title: Database Management Systems

cb.title: Database Systems: A Practical Approach to Design, Implementation, and Management
cb.listed_in_course_files: the CSC 472 lecture notes, which cite its DreamHome case study (Chapter 11), Section 12.7 and Figure 13.9

introduction-to-database-systems.why: Why a DBMS, levels of abstraction and data independence.

er-modelling.read: Chapter 11 (the DreamHome case study) and Chapter 12 (entity-relationship modelling)
er-modelling.why: The lecture notes refer to these chapters for requirements and ER modelling.

advanced-er-design.read: Chapter 12 (structural constraints, Section 12.7 on connection traps) and Chapter 13 (enhanced ER modelling)
advanced-er-design.why: The source of the lecture's multiplicity, fan and chasm traps, and specialization examples.

relational-model-and-algebra.read: Chapter 3: The Relational Model; Chapter 4: Relational Algebra and Calculus
relational-model-and-algebra.why: Keys, foreign keys, referential integrity actions, algebra and calculus.

sql.why: Basic, nested and aggregate queries, with the Sailors examples used in the notes.

normalization-and-physical-design.read: Chapter 19: Schema Refinement and Normal Forms; Chapter 8: Overview of Storage and Indexing; Chapter 20: Physical Database Design and Tuning
normalization-and-physical-design.why: Functional dependencies and normal forms, then files, indexes and physical design.

transactions-concurrency-and-recovery.read: Chapter 16: Overview of Transaction Management; Chapter 17: Concurrency Control; Chapter 18: Crash Recovery
transactions-concurrency-and-recovery.why: ACID, serializability, two-phase locking, timestamps and recovery.
